summary_of_pdf: This instrument is a certified digital transmission receipt generated by RMail, serving as evidentiary proof that a formal notice of proprietary rights and pending patent claims under 35 U.S.C. § 154(d) was successfully delivered to and downloaded by Antonio Filosa of Stellantis. The underlying transmission asserts intellectual property rights concerning vehicular optical data buses, vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) optical communication, and autonomous fleet logistics against multiple major automotive manufacturers.
attorneys_comments: From an evidentiary standpoint, this RMail download notice is highly probative for establishing 'actual notice' under 35 U.S.C. § 154(d), a strict statutory prerequisite for the accrual of provisional royalty rights prior to patent issuance. The time-stamped confirmation of file downloads by a senior executive at Stellantis effectively neutralizes any prospective defense of ignorance regarding the pending claims. Procedurally, this instrument should be authenticated under Federal Rule of Evidence 901(b)(9) and preserved as a business record under Rule 803(6). Tactically, while the delivery to Mr. Filosa establishes corporate receipt, the inclusion of multiple competitors (Tesla, GM, Ford, etc.) in the subject line risks characterizing the communication as a generalized industry broadcast rather than a particularized infringement notice. Counsel must ensure that the downloaded attachments contain sufficiently detailed claim-to-product mapping to satisfy the rigorous notice requirements of the Federal Circuit.
recommended_next_steps: 1. Institute a strict litigation hold on the original RMail transmission, the receipt, and all associated cryptographic delivery proofs to ensure admissibility under FRE 901. 2. Monitor the prosecution of the referenced USPTO applications to ensure claims issuing are substantially identical to those in the published applications, as required by 35 U.S.C. § 154(d)(2). 3. Draft a supplemental, highly particularized communication directed to Stellantis's Chief Legal Officer, enclosing preliminary claim charts mapping the pending claims to specific Stellantis platforms, thereby fortifying the foundation for willful infringement and enhanced damages under 35 U.S.C. § 284.
